primitives.name: Ball Liveliness Regime Shift
primitives.verbatim_quote: # MLB ball-liveliness calibration note (2026-09-24) Source: IG save @dugoutforever 2026-06-24 — "Is MLB juicing the balls again?" Cites a Sean Zerillo (Action Network) analysis: the baseball may have changed mid-season; MLB announced nothing; the numbers fueled speculation the ball got livelier.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L(t)': 'dimensionless liveliness index at time t', 't': 'temporal epoch in days since season start', 'R(t)': 'home run rate per game at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: Mid-season change in ball properties causes abrupt shift in R(t); MLB data lacks explicit announcement of such change.
primitives.breakdown_regime: t ∈ [0, T/2) ∪ (T/2, T], where T is season length

layer2.mapping: Empirical regression of R(t) against L(t) reveals discontinuity at t = T/2, indicating regime change in ball dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: HR rate deviation from expected baseline post-T/2

primitives.name: Context Matrix Drift
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the ball changes mid-season, any totals prior trained on early-season data drifts — this is exactly the "context matrix / regime change" problem the v5.3.0 build spec's Workstream 5 covers.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C(t)': 'context matrix at time t', 'D_e': 'early-season training data', 'D_l': 'late-season validation data'}
primitives.assumptions: Model trained on D_e becomes misaligned with D_l due to ball-liveliness shift.
primitives.breakdown_regime: C(t) ≠ C(t') for t, t' in different halves of season

layer2.mapping: Context matrix C(t) evolves under regime-shifted ball dynamics; drift quantified by KL divergence between D_e and D_l distributions.
layer2.telemetry: KL divergence between pre- and post-regime data distributions

primitives.name: Regime Change Covariate
primitives.verbatim_quote: If real: file it as a regime-change covariate in the context matrix (ball-batch era flag on MLB totals).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B(t)': 'ball-batch indicator function', 't_0': 'mid-season transition point', 'E': 'empirical evidence flag'}
primitives.assumptions: Ball-batch era B(t) is binary: 0 before t_0, 1 after t_0; E encodes verification status.

layer2.mapping: Introduce B(t) into model inputs to adjust for regime change; E ensures conditional update of model priors.
layer2.telemetry: Binary flag B(t) toggled at t_0 with E = 1 upon verification

The ball-liveliness regime shift is modeled as a temporal discontinuity in the home run rate R(t), induced by an unannounced change in physical properties of MLB baseballs. This manifests as a drift in the context matrix C(t), which encodes environmental and mechanical variables affecting game outcomes. The drift is detected through regression diagnostics comparing early vs. late-season data. A derived kernel maps this to a binary regime-change covariate B(t), which modifies model priors in GSE’s situational reasoning engine. The failure mode occurs when the model assumes stationarity, leading to systematic bias in predictions. Dualities arise between empirical observation and theoretical modeling, where the former provides the signal and the latter offers the structure to interpret it.
